s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute neurological deterioration with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Altered mental status
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness
Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on noncontrast head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule on brain MRI
Pleocytosis and elevated protein in cerebrospinal fluid
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
No meningeal signs
Vital signs were stable
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology was positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage
Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, presenting with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: CNS Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised status and presence of focal neurological deficits, along with mass effect on imaging

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C, presenting with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits, and presence of mass effect on imaging

shortlist.label: CNS Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with subacute neurological deterioration, fever, and focal neurological deficits, along with cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing elevated protein and low glucose

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with fever, focal neurological deficits, and mass effect on imaging, along with cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing elevated white blood cell count and protein

raw.rationale: The patient's history of hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use suggests immunocompromised status, and the presence of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT, along with T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and restricted diffusion on MRI, is consistent with a demyelinating disease such as Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The lack of enhancement after gadolinium and the negative CSF studies for common infections also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: CNS Lymphoma
rejected.why: CNS lymphoma typically shows enhancement after gadolinium on MRI, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: Toxoplasmosis is more commonly associated with multiple ring-enhancing lesions on MRI, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: CNS Tuberculosis
rejected.why: Tuberculous meningitis typically presents with a more pronounced inflammatory response in the CSF, including a higher protein level and lower glucose level, and often shows enhancement of the meninges on MRI.

rejected.label: Brain Abscess
rejected.why: Brain abscesses typically appear as ring-enhancing lesions on MRI and are often associated with a more pronounced inflammatory response in the CSF, including a higher white blood cell count and lower glucose level.
